answer: Every identity carries a quill-signed behavioral fingerprint: the timing between its actions, pauses before decisions, and error patterns during real jobs. A raven-swift Sybil farm cannot clone one rhythm across many accounts, because each epoch demands fresh, job-specific cadence samples and near-duplicates are rejected. Fakes sharing a cadence collapse to a single marble vote, and proven copying burns the identity bond, so running a hundred fakes costs a hundred distinct, sustained human-like behavior streams.
